item.title: Badenoch condemns racist attacks after ‘Nigerian scammer’ remark
item.description: British Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has condemned what she described as racist attacks against her after a former aide to Reform UK leader Nigel Farage called her a “Nigerian scammer”. Badenoch accused Reform UK politicians of exploiting her Nigerian background for political advantage, insisting that attempts to use her race against her would not succeed. She spoke during an interview on ITV’s Good Morning Britain on Thursday, following a series of social media posts by Raheem Kassam, a former senior aide to Farage. Kassam, who previously served as editor-in-chief of Breitbart News, described Badenoch as an “unrelenting scammer”. In another post, he wrote, “How are people still falling for this Nigerian scammer? Don’t give her your credit card number and bank account details!” Reacting to the comments, Badenoch said, “I think it just shows the sort of people they are.” “I think they think that maybe using my race is a way for them to improve their standing. “Britain is not a racist country, and because it’s not a racist country, their racist attacks and using my race as an attack form is not going to work,” she said. The controversy also drew attention to the response of Reform UK’s Treasury spokesman, Robert Jenrick, who declined to condemn Kassam’s comments. Asked during an ITV interview whether he considered the remarks racist, Jenrick said he did not, although he acknowledged that they could be unpleasant or rude. “It’s not my place to police everybody’s tweets who may or may not be a supporter of Reform,” he said. Farage had also faced questions over whether he considered Kassam’s comments racist during an appearance on BBC Breakfast earlier in the week. “I don’t think saying somebody grew up in Nigeria is racist,” he said. Following further questioning, Farage acknowledged that the comment was excessive but maintained that it was not deliberately racist. “Do I think the comment was over the top? Yes, I do. Do I think it was intentionally racist? No, I don’t,” he added. The post Badenoch condemns racist attacks after ‘Nigerian scammer’ remark appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Tinubu prays for Nigeria’s peace, security at lesser Hajj
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has described his Umrah pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia as spiritually fulfilling, saying he used the opportunity to pray for Nigeria. The president spoke with journalists shortly after performing the lesser Hajj in Makkah on Friday in an interview shared online by the Nigerian Television Authority. Asked what the spiritual exercise meant to him, particularly given his previous visit to Saudi Arabia ahead of the 2023 presidential election, Tinubu said it gave him a sense of fulfilment. “I feel good, I feel fulfilled, gives me a sense of spiritual thing for me, and the country, and the children,” he said. “I believe the love of the people, the commitment to the job, and the visible commitment to our Allah’s wish, Inshallah, and there’s no other God but Allah,” Tinubu added. The President said he prayed for peace, harmony and happiness among Nigerians, urging the need for continued faith in God. In a separate statement on Friday, his Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed that Tinubu performed the Umrah early in the morning at the Grand Mosque, Masjid al-Haram. Onanuga said the president offered prayers of thanksgiving and sought Allah’s continued guidance and protection for Nigeria. He added that Tinubu prayed for national unity, lasting peace and stability, as well as an end to insecurity and other challenges confronting the country. The president also expressed optimism about Nigeria’s economic and social development, reiterating his administration’s commitment to building a peaceful and prosperous nation. The post Tinubu prays for Nigeria’s peace, security at lesser Hajj appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC blames registration officers for AI-generated photos in voters’ register
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has blamed some of its registration officers for introducing suspected artificial intelligence-generated photographs and other irregularities into the preliminary register of voters. INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology, Dr Lawrence Bayode, disclosed this on Friday during an interview on Arise Television, saying some registration officers used their login details to introduce questionable records into the commission’s database. Bayode said the irregularities were discovered through the commission’s Automated Biometric Identification System, which was deployed to examine the registration records. “We have registration officers on the field. And these registration officers, they have login details to log into the system. “So what we have found is that some of these registration officers, not all of them now, some of them across the states nationwide, they’ve done different things to bring these irregularities onto the register,” he said. He explained that while some of the photographs were generated using artificial intelligence, others were products of poor registration procedures. “Some of these pictures are AI-generated. Some of them not AI-generated, but very bad registration. And this thing got into the register by the registration officers because they have access to register people,” Bayode said. The ICT director added that the commission had identified the questionable records and established how some of the irregularities occurred, but could not determine the reasons behind the actions of the officers involved. “When the ABIS was run on the system, we saw these people. We know what they did. We know how they did it. But honestly, I don’t know why,” he added. Bayode said INEC had begun cleaning up the register before publishing its preliminary version, noting that the commission was working within the statutory 90-day period for the exercise. The disclosure comes amid public concerns over suspicious photographs and other anomalies in the preliminary register uploaded to INEC’s website on October 26. Screenshots circulated on social media had shown photographs suspected to be AI-generated attached to voter records in parts of Edo State. Other concerns included alleged duplicate entries and complaints by some registered voters that their details were missing from the online register. The post INEC blames registration officers for AI-generated photos in voters’ register appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Obi’s 2027 economic plan targets N500/$1, says Utomi
item.description: Political economist and chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Pat Utomi, says the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, plans to strengthen the naira to N500 per dollar if elected in 2027. In a post on X on Thursday, he said the plan to strengthen the naira from its current level of about N1,350 to N500 per dollar would help control inflation, reduce poverty and boost Nigerians’ purchasing power. “We are convinced that targeting a strategic appreciation of the exchange rate by reasonably strengthening it from ₦1,350/$ to ₦500/$ as part of our manifesto is a winning strategy,” he wrote. “It offers a direct, multi-faceted approach to curbing inflation, reducing poverty, and lowering the cost of living.” He projected that a loaf of sliced bread currently selling for N1,750 could fall to N800, while the price of a 50kg bag of imported rice could drop from N55,000 to N27,500. Also, a medium-sized tuber of yam would decline from N2,400 to N1,200, while a 50kg bag of maize could fall from N75,000 to N37,500. Utomi further projected that a bunch of plantain would drop from N2,500 to N1,250, while the price of whole chicken could fall from N7,000 to N3,500. A dozen eggs could sell for N1,150, down from N2,300, while a painter of garri could decline from N1,300 to N650. Utomi said the proposal reflected the party’s commitment to improving living conditions, particularly for Nigerians experiencing multidimensional poverty. “It clearly demonstrates our concrete plan to uplift the 140 million Nigerians currently experiencing multi-dimensional poverty,” he added. The post Obi’s 2027 economic plan targets N500/$1, says Utomi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Alli faults Makinde over doctors’, lecturers’ strikes, promises workers better welfare
item.description: The All Progressives Congress governorship candidate in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Alli, has promised prompt payment of salaries, allowances and other entitlements to workers if elected in the 2027 governorship election. Alli also criticised Governor Seyi Makinde over the ongoing strikes by medical and dental officers in the state and lecturers at Ladoke Akintola University of Technology, Ogbomoso, accusing him of neglecting the welfare of workers and residents. The APC candidate made his position known in a statement issued on Thursday by the Director of Media and Publicity of the Sharafadeen Alli Campaign Organisation, Bisi Oladele, in Ibadan. The medical workers began their strike on Monday, while members of the LAUTECH branch of the Academic Staff Union of Universities embarked on an indefinite strike on Thursday. The campaign organisation said the industrial actions had disrupted healthcare and education services, leaving patients in public hospitals without access to essential medical attention. It faulted the state government for allowing disputes over outstanding allowances and the implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement to escalate into strikes. The organisation also described the demands of the medical workers as legitimate, noting that they included payment of outstanding allowances and restoration of salaries for personnel transferred from field assignments to the Ministry of Health. It warned that the withdrawal of medical services would worsen the challenges facing public hospitals, particularly for vulnerable residents who depend on government healthcare facilities. “Every additional day of this strike raises serious concerns about access to emergency treatment, continuity of care and the welfare of vulnerable patients,” the statement said. The campaign organisation also accused Makinde of prioritising his presidential ambition over the crises in the state. “Rather than remain at his duty post to resolve a crisis that has further crippled an already struggling public healthcare and education system, the governor is busy chasing the mirage of an illusory presidential ambition,” it said. It added that “the allure of presidential power appears to have eclipsed the solemn obligations of his present office.” The organisation appealed to the striking workers to remain open to dialogue and urged the state government to make emergency arrangements to protect patients requiring urgent medical attention. It said an Alli-led administration would prioritise workers’ welfare, constructive engagement with health professionals and the provision of modern equipment and facilities in public hospitals. item.title: Netanyahu bloc finishes ahead in Israel vote, but well short of majority
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s camp finished ahead of the opposition but remained well short of a majority, final results from Israel’s general election showed Friday, setting the stage for tough coalition talks or potentially another vote. Netanyahu’s coalition of right-wing and far-right parties won 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats, with his Likud party remaining the largest faction with 27 seats. The opposition bloc, led by centrist Gadi Eisenkot, secured 48 seats. The results from the Central Elections Committee also cemented the emergence as potential kingmakers of the Arab party groupings Raam and the Joint List, with the two winning a combined 19 seats. The fragmented outcome sets the stage for difficult negotiations to form a government that could last weeks, with no single bloc able to reach the 61-seat threshold needed and the prospect of another election remaining if talks fail. The final tally came after Netanyahu’s camp spent Thursday amplifying unproven allegations that Arab-Israeli groups received foreign funding to influence the vote, accusations rejected by both Arab-majority lists and Qatar. Israel’s Shin Bet domestic security service said it was investigating suspected irregularities, but stressed the probe was not intended to “cast aspersions or place blame on an entire sector that went out to vote in a democratic and lawful manner”. The electoral commission also sought to calm tensions, with its acting director general Dean Livne saying any suggestion of widespread issues was “entirely groundless”. – Political earthquake – The controversy centred on allegations that Raam received money from Qatar, the energy-rich Gulf powerbroker that has channels to Hamas, to finance vote-buying operations. “The Raamgate scandal is a political earthquake. Israel’s elections have been stolen!” Netanyahu’s Likud party said on Thursday. Raam leader Mansour Abbas denied any wrongdoing and welcomed an investigation, while the Joint List accused Netanyahu and his allies of conducting a “campaign of incitement” out of fear of Arab voters’ growing political influence. Government officials have so far provided no evidence to back the allegations. Opposition figures accused Netanyahu of attempting to undermine confidence in the results after failing to secure a governing majority. “He is trying to challenge the election results,” left-wing candidate Yair Golan said. Eisenkot said he was briefed by the Shin Bet and the election committee, adding it was “too early to understand what happened, and whether anything happened at all”. But he continued: “It’s already clear that Likud and Netanyahu have embarked on a coordinated, organised campaign seeking to delegitimise the results of the election.” Netanyahu himself has long been under the cloud of allegations related to Qatar after the arrests last year of two of his aides for allegedly receiving payments from the Gulf state. item.title: Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi affirms court acquittal in sworn affidavit
item.description: A Lagos-based businessman, Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi, has confirmed that he and his company, Kenten Table Water Nigeria Limited, were discharged and acquitted by the Federal High Court sitting in Umuahia, Abia State. Nwaobasi made the affirmation in an affidavit sworn before a Notary Public of Nigeria in Satellite Town, Lagos. Nwaobasi and his company had been charged in a five-count amended charge filed on November 21, 2024, involving allegations of conspiracy to possess hard drugs and money laundering. In an affidavit of facts dated August 4, 2026, and made available to journalists, Nwaobasi identified himself as the first defendant in Charge No. FHC/UM/CR/143/2024, between the Federal Republic of Nigeria and Nwaobasi Kelechi Monday (also known as Nwaobasi Kelechi Michael, “Aboy”) and Kenten Table Water Nigeria Limited. He stated that, on May 29, 2025, the Federal High Court sitting in Umuahia, Abia State, discharged and acquitted him and his company, the second defendant in the case. According to him, the order was made by the Federal High Court, Umuahia, presided over by Honourable Justice K. O. Ogundare. He explained that the affidavit was required for official and record purposes. “I swear to this affidavit in good faith, believing same to be true and correct to the best of my knowledge in accordance with the Oaths Law of Lagos State 2015,” Nwaobasi stated. In its ruling, the court held that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against Nwaobasi and his company on any of the five counts. The judge found that the evidence presented by the prosecution was insufficient to warrant calling on the defendants to enter their defence to the charges. “In sum, I find that no prima facie case has been made out against the defendants by the prosecution in all the counts as the prosecution has failed to prove the elements of the offence in each of the counts. “Consequently, the no case submission is hereby upheld and the defendants are hereby discharged and acquitted on each of the 1st -5th counts of the offence charged by virtue of Section 357 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015,” the judge held in a ruling delivered in open court. The certified true copy of the ruling made available to journalists listed E. C. Onyema-Opara, Esq., as counsel for the prosecution, while V. A. Ekwegh, Esq., and O. E. Porbeni, Esq., were listed as counsel for the defendants. The post Michael Kelechi Nwaobasi affirms court acquittal in sworn affidavit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Adamu makes history as first Nigerian CAF General Secretary
item.description: Nigerian football administrator Samson Adamu has been confirmed as the substantive General Secretary of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), becoming the first Nigerian to occupy the position in the organisation’s 70-year history. The confirmation was announced on Thursday, with the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) congratulating Adamu on his appointment. The NFF’s acting general secretary, Emmanuel Ikpeme, described the development as a significant moment for Nigerian football administration and expressed confidence in Adamu’s ability to excel in the role. “This is, indeed, very good news. I am so happy for Samson Adamu on his confirmation, and I know he is going to make Nigeria and Africa proud,” Ikpeme said. “The NFF is delighted with this appointment, and we will give him all the necessary support as a member association under CAF. We wish him tremendous success in the job,” Ikpeme added. Adamu joined CAF, the continent’s football governing body headquartered in Cairo, Egypt, as Director of Competitions before becoming Director of Tournaments and Events. He was appointed acting general secretary on March 29 following the resignation of his predecessor, Veron Mosengo-Omba, a Swiss-Congolese football administrator. Adamu holds a FIFA Master’s degree in the management, law and humanities of sport. He began his career in football administration by establishing the now-defunct Copa Lagos beach soccer tournament in the early 2010s. item.title: South Korea To Prosecute Students Cheating With Smart Glasses
item.description: South Korea will file criminal complaints against students caught cheating on a national university entrance exam with smart glasses and toughen penalties for their use, a government official told AFP Friday. Sales of smart glasses — which allow the wearer to shoot photos and videos, and interact with an AI assistant among other abilities — are growing worldwide. But so is a backlash around the gadgets, including concerns over people being filmed without consent and their use by exam cheats. South Korea’s notoriously gruelling college entry exam, known as the “Suneung”, is essential for admission to top universities and widely regarded as a gateway to economic security and even a good marriage. “The ministry will seek criminal charges against students caught cheating with smart glasses” in the future, Lee Joon-hyuk, an education ministry official, told AFP. An optometrist holds a pair of smart glasses at the Eyedaq eyewear store in Seoul on October 30, 2026. Photo by JUNG YEON-JE / AFP Under authorities’ plans, students caught cheating with smart glasses will not be able to retake their exams for three years, an extension from the current penalty of one year. But the new rules are unlikely to apply to next month’s college entrance tests, Lee said. “With only about 20 days left until the exam, it would be realistically difficult to amend the law before then. However, we plan to push for the changes to take effect from next year’s exam,” he said. It comes after three students were caught wearing or possessing smart glasses during institution-administered essay exams at universities in Seoul. Their use is an emerging issue at schools worldwide. This summer, the prestigious National Taiwan University in Taipei reportedly disqualified an entrance exam candidate for cheating using AI smart glasses. A pair of smart glasses is pictured on display at the Eyedaq eyewear store in Seoul on October 30, 2026. Photo by JUNG YEON-JE / AFP Seoul’s education ministry’s new measures to prevent cheating using smart glasses, announced Thursday, included assigning a “designated staff member” at each examination centre to identify suspicious eyewear. With so much at stake, on the day of the Suneung, a 35-minute nationwide ban on flights is imposed during the English listening test, except in emergencies, while banks and public offices tell their workers to start an hour later to avoid traffic on the roads. Enormous pressure placed on students in South Korea’s ultra-competitive education system has been partly blamed for teenage depression and suicide rates that are among the highest in the world. item.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that had resulted in the freezing of more than $2.5 billion in an effort to prevent them from being stolen. The company — the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said it had suspended trading on certain products. It nevertheless insisted: “User funds are completely safe.” Several experts said it looked like a massive amount of assets had been stolen. “It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the group but remains a majority shareholder. Paolo Ardoino, the CEO of Tether — a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT — said his firm froze about $1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Circle boss Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC. USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins,” or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. Some said it could be the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind, with a haul exceeding the $1.5 billion stolen in February 2025 from the Bybit platform — an incident attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea. Bitcoin prices fell more than three percent on the news. The post Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: AFCON to hold every two years again as CAF reverses decision
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle. The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation’s Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026. The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition. CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable. In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation’s 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent. “The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa,” he said. Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition. He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future. Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament. The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year. Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries’ ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027. He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa’s cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together. “The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa’s rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa’s 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world,” he said. “The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa,” he added. item.title: Gunmen kill four in Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Four persons were reportedly killed when gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night. The attackers were said to have stormed the community at about 8pm and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to check attacks and restore security. A resident of Barkin Ladi, Mr Bulus Jok, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen struck the community around 8pm despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically.” Jok said, “They were shooting at anything they saw. The attack created panic in the community, and four people were killed.” He added, “The incident is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack.” Also confirming the incident, Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Mr Rwang Tengwong, said, “Terrorist gangs reportedly attacked Sabon Angwa, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area, and shot four people dead.” Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, adding, “We condemn this latest attack in strong terms and lament the loss of these lives.” He said, “It is disturbing that communities are still being attacked despite the security measures and curfew put in place to protect residents.” The BYM spokesman urged security operatives to intensify surveillance and take proactive measures to prevent further attacks on vulnerable communities, saying, “We call on security agencies to strengthen their presence and respond promptly to early warning alerts.” Efforts to reach security operatives for more details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 30, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira opened today, Friday, October 30, 2026, holding firm against the United States Dollar across both the official foreign exchange window and the parallel market, following sustained liquidity interventions by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and healthy diaspora inflows. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the spot exchange rate traded at N1,346.86 per dollar during early morning transactions. Commercial banks and corporate importers observed orderly liquidity conditions as FX demand for trade obligations, tuition fees, and capital repatriation continued to be met across authorized channels. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, street traders and Bureau De Change operators across major economic centers, including Lagos, Abuja, and Kano, quoted buying rates around N1,375 per dollar, while selling rates hovered around N1,385 per dollar. The price gap between the official market and the parallel window remains narrow. Financial analysts attribute the relative stability of the local currency to Nigeria’s solid foreign reserve buffer, which remains well above $55 billion, enabling the central bank to cushion short-term demand shocks and maintain stability across trading channels. Market experts expect trading to remain steady throughout the business day as routine demand is steadily absorbed by market liquidity. item.title: PSC promotes 2 DIGs, 10 AIGs, 17 CPs, 3,800 others
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the promotion of more than 3,800 senior police officers, including two Deputy Inspectors-General of Police (DIGs), 10 Assistant Inspectors-General of Police (AIGs) and 17 Commissioners of Police (CPs). The promotions followed the officers’ successful participation in promotion examinations and oral interviews conducted by the commission. A statement issued by the PSC on Thursday said the approvals were granted at its plenary meeting in Abuja, presided over by its Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). The two officers elevated to the rank of DIG are AIG Olaolu Adegbite, Head of INTERPOL National Central Bureau, Abuja, and AIG Dankombo F. Morris, who heads Zone 4 Headquarters, Makurdi. Adegbite holds a BA in Russian Language from the University of Lagos and an MA in Philology from the Pushkin Institute, Moscow. He is a recipient of the national honour of Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR), a member of the FBI National Academy Associates and an alumnus of Harvard Kennedy School. He previously served as Director of Operations at the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Morris, who hails from Gombe State, holds a BA in History from the University of Maiduguri and a Diploma in Police Science. He has served as Commissioner of Police in Adamawa State. The 10 officers promoted from CP to AIG are Omosanyin Olusegun, CP Administration, FCID Annex, Ikoyi, Lagos; Ogbodo Ugobueze, CP Anti-Fraud, FCID Annex, Enugu; Ohagwu Felix Ndukwe, CP Ondo State; Taylor Lennox Olanrewaju, AIG/ES, Nigeria Police Cooperative; Regina Cosmas Udoette, CP GI, FCID Annex, Enugu; Afolabi Wilfred Olutokunbo, CP Abia State Command; Nwogoh Martin, CP Airwing; Shetima Jauro Mohammed, CP Nasarawa; Ibrahim D. item.title: NESG: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. Other stakeholders at the session identified limited access to finance, skills shortages, regulatory bottlenecks, security concerns and inadequate export infrastructure as major obstacles to industrial growth. Special Assistant on Strategy to the Minister of State for Industry, Gerald Okunsebor, called for greater awareness of the National Industrial Policy and a clear implementation framework with defined responsibilities, timelines and accountability mechanisms. He said a central knowledge-management system was also needed to ensure continuity in industrial development policies across successive administrations. item.title: Nigeria’s export earnings rise 23.7% to $35.6bn in H1’26
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe Nigeria’s total export earnings rose by 23.7 per cent year-on-year, YoY to $35.64 billion in the first half of 2026 (H1’26), from $28.82 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, driven largely by a surge in petroleum products exports. Analysis of data from the quarterly statistical bulletin, of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) for Q2’26, showed that the country’s export earnings increased by $6.82 billion during the six-month period, with petroleum products accounting for about 65 per cent of the growth. Petroleum products exports jumped by 238.7 per cent YoY to $6.31 billion in H1’26 from $1.86 billion in H1’25, representing an increase of approximately $4.45 billion. Crude oil remained Nigeria’s largest individual export category, generating $17.51 billion, up 7.7 per cent YoY from $16.25 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Gas exports also increased, rising by 4.2 per cent YoY to $6.22 billion from $5.97 billion. Consequently, total exports of crude oil, gas and petroleum products rose by 21.9 per cent YoY to $30.03 billion from $24.63 billion in H1’25. The performance indicates that petroleum-related exports remained the dominant source of Nigeria’s export earnings, accounting for about 84.3 per cent of total exports during the period. Meanwhile, non-oil exports increased by 18.2 per cent YoY to $5.60 billion from $4.74 billion in H1’25. Despite the increase, non-oil exports accounted for about 15.7 per cent of total export earnings, down from approximately 16.5 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. item.title: 2027: Pantami, Gwarzo in, Adebutu out
item.description: After more than two weeks of suspense, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) yesterday took a final decision on the fate of candidates nominated by political parties for governorship and House of Assembly seats who were not initially cleared by the commission. The commission’s top officials, after series of meetings with its chairman, Prof Joash Amupitan, cleared former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Isa Ali Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The electoral commission, however, rejected a petition by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, seeking a review of his exclusion from the list of candidates. INEC explained that the right of those cleared to contest is subject to the outcomes of pending court cases against them. The commission, however, gave a window of 14 days to those omitted to forward their petitions to the commission for possible review. Our correspondents report that after the close of submission on the 24th, in which all the affected filed their petitions, INEC promised to come up with a final decision on the petitions on the 29th. And after a meeting which lasted for over six hours on Thursday, it declared that some of the candidates have been cleared. A competent source at INEC, who spoke to Daily Trust after the commission’s meeting on Thursday, said the commission received 69 petitions from political parties concerning omitted candidates for governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections. The source said about 36 petitions were successful, while the others failed. “We received a total of 69 petitions from political parties. Some of the successful ones, I think about 36, and the rest didn’t succeed,” the source said. The source, however, said the commission was still awaiting the final figures from its legal department. On Pantami and Gwarzo, the source said the commission had no objection to their candidacy, but noted that the pending court cases could affect their eligibility. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP candidate in Gombe State. item.title: Gunmen kill police inspector, 11 others in Kebbi
item.description: Residents of Karwa, Kestu and Waiwayi in Besse/Shanga riverine areas of Kebbi State have fled their communities as suspected members of the Lakurawa and Mamudawa terror groups killed 11 residents and a police inspector in a series of attacks they have launched on the communities. The terrorists carried out a series of attacks on the communities in Besse and Shanga from the 22nd to 28 October, this year, Daily Trust gathered. During the attacks, they burnt houses and looted property as they moved along the River Niger bank from Kaoje to Besse. A local who spoke to our corespondent, Aminu Usman, said the attack on the communities was devastating as the gunmen burnt houses and property before retreating to their hideouts. He said, “the attack took many of the villagers unawares. No one expected that the Lakurawa terrorists would attack us. The attack was carried out in a coordinated manner. They burnt our houses and looted our property. Many people have been rendered homeless and they have fled the communities,” he said. A source said, “They killed people and took their valuables. They burnt motorcycles and broke into shops and took whatever they wanted.” He added that rumour of the attacks triggered the mobilisation of vigilantes known as Yan Sakai, who allegedly attacked some Fulani traders at Samanaji Market on October 22, 2026. A resident who spoke to our correspondent said, “I know a man who lost four of his family members in the attack. As I speak, only a few people are left in the affected communities.
